literal.prompt: Какой город Пётр I сделал столицей России?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The Presidential Library states that St Petersburg became capital of the Russian Empire after the Northern War victory (L70,L73-L75). UNESCO states that Russia’s capital moved to St Petersburg in the early eighteenth century (L57). The four options are all Russian cities: the Novgorod Museum locates the historic Trade Side of Veliky Novgorod across the Volkhov bridge (L217-L220); UNESCO names Moscow and Pskov as Russian cities with central kremlins/citadels (L24-L27,L67); the Presidential Library identifies St Petersburg as the founded city and capital (L73-L78).
literalGroups.locator: Presidential Library L70,L73-L78; UNESCO L24-L27,L57,L67; Novgorod Museum L217-L220.

literalGroups.literal: При Петре I столицей стал Санкт-Петербург. Правительство переехало туда из Москвы в начале XVIII века.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Presidential Library states that St Petersburg became the capital of the Russian Empire after the victory in the Northern War (L70,L73-L75). UNESCO states that Russia’s capital moved from Moscow to St Petersburg in the early eighteenth century (L57).

literalGroups.literal: Великий Новгород — древний русский город на реке Волхов.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Novgorod State Museum describes Veliky Novgorod as an ancient town of medieval Rus (L217), and identifies the bridge over the Volkhov leading to the city’s Trade Side, where a princely court and old market stood since Yaroslav the Wise (L220). This supports the note’s city, river and historic-trade claims.

The Presidential Library states that Peter chose an islet site for the fortress and explains that the city was called Saint Petersburg, meaning the city of Saint Peter (L76-L78). This is an own-option etymological fact beyond the prompt and key.

literalGroups.literal: Московский Кремль был великокняжеской, а затем царской резиденцией.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO’s Russian description says that Moscow Kremlin was first a grand-princely and then a royal residence (L24-L27).

literalGroups.literal: Псков — древнерусский город с кремлём-цитаделью в центре.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO identifies Pskov among Old Russian towns whose central kremlin is a citadel (L67). The note is phrased to match that limited claim.
